shortName: Ostergaard v. Microsoft Corp.
citation: Ostergaard et al v. Microsoft Corporation
summary: Three residents of Mount Pleasant/Sturtevant, Wisconsin — Garret Ostergaard, David Wade, and Joy Wade — filed a putative class-action lawsuit against Microsoft, alleging that noise from its 1.2-million-square-foot "Fairwater" data center constitutes a continuing physical invasion and nuisance affecting more than 1,000 households within a 1.5-mile radius. The complaint, filed July 1, 2026, attributes the noise to the facility's cooling fans and other equipment, alleges the disruption has cost Ostergaard sleep and forced a work-shift change and has prevented the Wades from enjoying their backyard, and claims Microsoft was aware of the noise but failed to adequately mitigate it; plaintiffs seek class certification and damages, with the suit estimating potential damages exceeding $5 million.

shortName: Paulus v. Citicorp North America, Inc.
citation: Paulus v. Citicorp North America, Inc.
summary: Delaware County, Ohio homeowner Kurt Paulus and his wife sued Citicorp North America, Citigroup Inc., and Citigroup Technology, alleging that generator noise from Citicorp's data center near U.S. Route 23 — which Paulus documented by tracking activation times and recording decibel levels from his bedroom — disrupted sleep and enjoyment of his property in a previously quiet, wooded residential area. Paulus, an engineer, stated he sought to resolve the issue directly with the company before filing suit, noting that Ohio law leaves townships without authority to regulate noise from commercial or industrially zoned property.

shortName: 1778 Rich Pike LLC v. Clifton Twp. Zoning
citation: 1778 Rich Pike LLC vs. Clifton Twp Pa Zoning
summary:
1778 Rich Pike LLC appealed the Clifton Township Zoning Hearing Board's November 19, 2025 decision to the Lackawanna County Court of Common Pleas. The Board had denied the developer's substantive validity challenge to the township's zoning ordinance, which the developer argued excluded data center uses. The appeal contends that data center uses are legitimate land uses entitled to zoning accommodation under state law, that the ordinance fails to define or classify data center uses and is therefore exclusionary, that the ordinance lacks any comparable use to which data centers could be analogized, and that it provides no reasonable path to approval by special exception.

**Sources:**
- Land-use appeal, _1778 Rich Pike LLC v. Clifton Twp. Zoning Hearing Bd._, No. 2025-CV-09492 (Lackawanna Cnty. C.P. filed Dec. 1, 2025) — primary filing not accessible; date per news account sourced to the filing itself
